title: Reconcile token undercount caused by interleaved prefetch + reconnect replay
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Several Dedicated and Private tenants reported missing token usage on invoices after a cluster failover/agent reconnect window. Symptoms: end-to-end session logs showed streamed responses completed to customers, but the accounting ledger reflected an intermittent undercount (~3-12% depending on workload) for requests that included aggressive prefetching + streaming resume. Affected customers opened escalation tickets citing surprise credits on their month-end bills. This ticket coordinates diagnosis, reconciliation, patching, and customer comms.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a long streaming completion with prefix prefetch enabled (kv-prefetch=true) and aggressive batch windowing.
2) Simulate a short proxy reconnect / node handoff (TCP reconnect + session rebind).
3) Allow client to resume stream with existing client-side retry-id but new backend connection id.
4) Observe final token accounting: generated tokens on runtime trace exist but ledger ingestion shows fewer tokens.
Expected: tokens consumed during resumed stream are attributed and persisted exactly once. Actual: some resumed fragments are not emitted to the ledger due to replay dedup logic interacting with prefetch markers.
root_cause: During reconnect/rebind the streaming proxy reissued prefetch frames to warm KV and prime continuous batching. The accounting path deduped frames using an idempotency key derived from connection-level metadata; when the proxy presented warmed fragments from prefetch with a different connection id but same client-side retry token, the ledger ingestion classified them as prefetched (no-charge) and later dropped re-emitted tokens on final commit, resulting in undercount. Interaction between prefetch marker state, streaming resume path, and ledger emitter batching caused the gap.
proposed_fix: 1) Change idempotency key derivation to be stable across reconnects by hashing client_retry_token + request_id instead of connection_id. 2) Ensure prefetch frames are tagged with explicit chargeable boolean set only by runtime after final emit. 3) Add a reconciliation hedging pass in the ledger emitter to validate runtime completion traces against emitted ledger rows and emit compensating deltas for mismatches during backfills. 4) Add a short-term emergency backfill job for affected tenants.
rollout_plan: 1) Patch runtime and proxy (branch: fix/stream-prefetch-idempotency) and run canary against internal staging workload. 2) Canary in hosted & dedicated with 1 region, monitor 24h. 3) Expand to remaining regions if no regressions. 4) Run per-tenant reconciliation for last 30 days in parallel; apply compensating credits where verified. 5) Notify customers after reconciliation complete. Target full rollout by runtime-1.26.3.
tests: Unit tests for idempotency key derivation; integration test simulating reconnect with prefetch frames; end-to-end ledger roundtrip tests to assert emitted tokens == runtime-traced tokens; chaos test injecting reconnects during streaming to ensure no undercount.
monitoring: Add new metric: accounting.unmatched_fragment_rate (count of runtime fragments with no ledger row within ingestion window). Dashboards: metering -> undercount-alerts; set alert when unmatched_fragment_rate > 0.5% over 10m for a tenant. Add tracing tags on stream resume path for quick trace->ledger correlation.
communication:
- Customer-facing: templated explanation + reconciliation offer; send targeted emails to affected tenants by 2026-03-22.
- Internal: update billing ops and finance with reconciliation plan, include list of impacted invoices.
- Postmortem: publish incident writeup and RCA to Confluence after full reconciliation complete.
